BURHAN:v1p206/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.speaker: عائشة
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.claim: The beginning-of-revelation report in al-Bukhari, explicitly authenticated by al-Hakim from Aisha, establishes اقرأ as the first revelation; Muslim gives it through “He taught man what he did not know.”
BURHAN:v1p206/r1.anchor: وأخرجه الحاكم فى مستدركه من حديث عائشة رضى الله عنها صريحا وقال صحيح الإسناد

ITQAN:v1p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.claim: Ubayd b. ʿUmayr says Gabriel brought the Prophet a silk sheet and told him to recite; he identifies the opening of al-ʿAlaq as the first sura sent down.
ITQAN:v1p75/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أشتة في كتاب المصاحف عن عبيد بن عمير قال جاء جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بنمط فقال اقرأ

ITQAN:v1p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.speaker: الزهري
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.claim: Al-Zuhrī recounts that while the Prophet was at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought a silk sheet inscribed with the opening verses of al-ʿAlaq.
ITQAN:v1p75/r2.anchor: وأخرج عن الزهري أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتى ملك بنمط من ديباج فيه مكتوب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.claim: The name al-ʿAlaq points to creation and return: whoever knows they were made from a clot can recognize God's power to recreate them from dust, which is more receptive to life.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r3.anchor: والعلق يدل على كل من النهاية ثم البداية بالالتزام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478/r4.claim: The clot is singled out as the material that carries life, which is why the soul itself is called a life-bearing substance.

BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r3.claim: Humanity is singled out either for its wondrous creation or its nobility as the recipient of revelation; the first creation clause may be broad and the second an explanation.
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r3.anchor: على الاول تخصيص لخلق الانسان بالذكر من بين سائر المخلوقات لاستقلاله ببدآئع الصنع

BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r4.claim: علق is the plural of علقة, a clinging, moist clot of congealed blood; the plural treats generic humanity collectively and suits the verse endings.
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r4.anchor: جمع علقة كثمر وثمرة وهى الدم الجامد

BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r5.claim: The clot highlights the striking gap between humanity's first state and final form, proving divine power; human creation is a primary blessing and evidence of God's existence, knowledge, and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v10p363#2/r5.anchor: لبيان كمال قدرته تعالى باظهار ما بين حالته الأولى والآخرة من التباين البين

QASHANI:96:1-2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:96:1-2/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:96:1-2/r3.claim: Human is singled out after general creation because the Prophet was returned to the composite human form and veiling required for revelation, descent, and prophethood.
QASHANI:96:1-2/r3.anchor: ولما رده إلى الخلقية في صورة الجمعية الإنسانية وأمره بالاحتجاب بها لتمكن الوحي والتنزيل والنبوة خص الخلق

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r6.claim: ʿAlaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, like shajar and shajara; a ʿalaqa is congealed blood, and when it flows it is shed blood.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r6.anchor: العلق جمع علقة ؛ كشجر وشجرة . . ( والعلقة الدم الجامد فإذا جرى فهو المسفوح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.claim: Aisha narrates in the two Sahihs that Gabriel came to Muhammad in Hira, commanded him three times, embraced him forcefully each time, then recited the opening through 'what he did not know.'
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r3.anchor: وفي حديث ( الصحيحين ) عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قولها فيه : ( حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.claim: Aisha's narration is directly from the Prophet; her account that he returned trembling with the passage means he retained and recited what had been dictated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r4.anchor: فهذا الحديث روته عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لقولها قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.claim: Khadija's request that Waraqa hear him further indicates Muhammad recited the revealed passage immediately; Gabriel's repeated command repeated God's wording to accustom him to reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p435/r5.anchor: وهذا ينبىء بأن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عندما قيل له بعد الفطة الثالثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r2.claim: 'Created the human from a clot' may be a detailed apposition to general creation, a partitive apposition if the first object is broad, or an explanation specifying that God created humans from clots.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r2.anchor: وجملة { خلق الإنسان من علق } يجوز أن تكون بدلا من جملة { الذي خلق }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r4.claim: Humans are singled out because each person readily reflects on their own origin, making it a compelling proof of the Creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p437/r4.anchor: وخص خلق الإنسان بالذكر من بين بقية المخلوقات لأنه المطرد في مقام الاستدلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r1.claim: The verse implicitly censures polytheists for missing the proof of divine unity present in their own selves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r1.anchor: وفيه تعريض بتحميق المشركين الذين ضلوا عن توحيد الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r2.claim: The clot points to wondrous stages and qualities that make humanity sovereign over earthly creation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r2.anchor: وفي قوله : { من علق } إشارة إلى ما ينطوي في أصل خلق الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r3.claim: Alaq is the collective name for analaqah: a fingernail-sized, dark red, moist clot, named for resemblance to a small freshwater leech that attaches to animals and sucks blood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r3.anchor: والعلق : اسم جمع علقة وهي قطعة قدر الأنملة من الدم الغليظ الجامد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r4.claim: After male and female fluids unite and time passes, they become a clot; it marks the start of formation because the male fluid alone cannot produce an embryo.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r4.anchor: ومعنى : { خلق الإنسان من علق } أن نطفة الذكر ونطفة المرأة بعد الاختلاط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r5.claim: The clot's later development into maturity encodes hidden capacities, especially the ability to gain knowledge and write.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r5.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن خلق الإنسان من علق ثم مصيره إلى كمال أشده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur calls mention of the clot a scientific miracle: the microscopic fertilized ovum develops in fluid, resembling a leech in size, blood color, and suspension, unless impeded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r6.anchor: ومن إعجاز القرآن العلمي ذكر العلقة لأن الثابت في العلم الآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p438/r7.claim: The preposition min denotes a starting point.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.claim: The opening five verses gather divine attributes: lordship implies existence and oneness, creation and teaching indicate acts, and al-Akram entails perfection and freedom from deficiency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p439/r7.anchor: وقد جمعت هذه الآيات الخمس من أول السورة أصول الصفات الإلاهية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.claim: These are the final five verses of the passage first revealed at Hira; the following discussion on verses 6–10 begins a new subject.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p441/r6.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r6.claim: The human being's creation is a striking sign through intellect, perception, bodily ligaments, and bones; ʿalaq is plural of ʿalaqa, a small piece of blood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p501#3/r6.anchor: وخلقة الإنسان من أعظم العبر حتى أنه ليس في المخلوقات التي لدينا أكثر عبرا منه في عقله وإدراكه ورباطات بدنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r1.claim: Al-insan is a generic term that also evokes all animals; the verse does not point to Adam, created from clay, since that origin was not established in the hearers' beliefs, so it mentions the familiar offspring instead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p502/r1.anchor: اسم الجنس، ويمشي الذهن معه إلى جميع الحيوان، وليست الإشارة إلى آدم، لأنه مخلوق من طين،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r5.claim: Human here means Adam's children, and alaq is the plural of alaqa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r5.anchor: والإنسان هاهنا ابن آدم والعلق جمع علقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r6.claim: Al-Farra explains the plural alaq as agreement with the generic plural sense of human and with the rhyming verse endings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p175/r6.anchor: لما كان الإنسان في معنى الجمع جمع العلق مع مشاكلة رؤوس الآيات

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r1.claim: Aisha recounts the beginning of revelation: the Prophet first saw true dreams, then loved retreat and worship at Hira, where Gabriel commanded him to read and pressed him three times before revealing the opening verses.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت : أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r2.speaker: خديجة
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r2.claim: Khadija reassures the shaken Prophet that God will never disgrace him, citing his kinship care, truthful speech, support of the burdened, hospitality, and aid in hardship.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r2.anchor: فقالت له : كلا أبشر فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبدا ؛ إنك لتصل الرحم ،   وتصدُق الحديث

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r3.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r3.claim: Waraqa identifies the visitor as the messenger who came to Moses, predicts the Prophet will be driven out, and wishes he could live to support him.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r3.anchor: فقال ورقة : هذا الناموس الذي أنزل على موسى

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir says this report is transmitted in both Sahih collections and notes that he discussed its chain, text, and meanings at length in his Bukhari commentary.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r4.anchor: وهذا الحديث مخرج في الصحيحين من حديث الزهري

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r5.claim: These opening verses were the first Qur'an revealed, the first mercy and blessing to humanity; they recall creation from a clot and God's honoring of people by teaching what they did not know, the distinction by which Adam excelled the angels.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r5.anchor: وهُنَّ أول رحمة رَحم الله بها العباد ،   وأول نعمة أنعم الله بها عليهم .   وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r6.claim: Knowledge takes mental, spoken, and written forms; written knowledge entails the other two, while mental or spoken knowledge need not be written.
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r6.anchor: والعلم تارة يكون في الأذهان ،   وتارة يكون في اللسان ،   وتارة يكون في الكتابة بالبنان

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r7.claim: An aphorism urges preserving knowledge by writing it down.

IBNKATHIR:96:2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:2/r8.claim: Another aphorism says that whoever acts on what he knows will be granted knowledge of what he did not know.

FARRA:v3p278/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p278/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p278/r2.claim: Although ʿalaqa is singular, the verse uses the plural ʿalaq because “human” is collective and the form matches the rhyme.
FARRA:v3p278/r2.anchor: وإنما هي علقة، لأن الإنسان في معنى جمع، فذهب بالعلق إلى الجمع لمشاكلة رءوس الآيات.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan and has seventeen verses.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r6.claim: ʿAlaq is a moist clot that adheres to what it touches; when it dries it is no longer ʿalaq, and the plural reflects that insan is generic.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r6.anchor: والعلق: القطعة من الدم تتعلق بما يمر به لرطوبتها، فإذا جفت فليست بعلق،

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.speaker: عائشة ومجاهد وعطاء بن يسار
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.claim: One report says the first revelation from the Qur'an was Iqraʾ bismi rabbik.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r10.anchor: قيل: أول ما نزل من القرآن: (اقرأ باسم ربك)، عن عائشة، ومجاهد، وعطاء بن يسار.

JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.speaker: جماعة من المفسرين
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.claim: Another report says the first five verses descended first, while the rest of the surah came later; a similar report is attributed to ʿĀʾisha.
JISHUMI:v10p7475/r11.anchor: وقيل: أول ما نزل منها خمس آيات إلى قوله: (ما لم يعلم)، ثم نزل باقي السورة بعد ذلك

JISHUMI:v10p7477/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r8.claim: The clot is mentioned among human stages because it is the most lowly origin, magnifying God's power and blessing in bringing humanity to perfection and urging gratitude and worship.
JISHUMI:v10p7477/r8.anchor: وإنما ذكر العلقة وإن كان له أحوال أخر؛ لأنه أدخل في الاستخفاف

KASHSHAF:96:2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:2/r1.claim: Humans are singled out among created things because revelation is addressed to them and they are earth's noblest creatures.
KASHSHAF:96:2/r1.anchor: تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق

KASHSHAF:96:2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the vague Creator is specified as the one who made humanity to magnify the wonder of human formation.
KASHSHAF:96:2/r2.anchor: فقيل : { الذي خَلَقَ } مبهماً ،   ثم فسره

KASHSHAF:96:2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:2/r3.claim: The plural clots means humanity generically, as in the cited verse, though an individual was created from one clot.
KASHSHAF:96:2/r3.anchor: لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع ،   كقوله : { إِنَّ الإنسان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r4.claim: Mentioning humans singles them out as revelation's recipient and earth's noblest creature, or explains the initially unspecified Creator's marvelous creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r4.anchor: وقوله : { خلق الإنسان } تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r5.claim: The plural “clots” is used although each human begins from a clot because humankind is a collective, as in 103:2.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p781/r5.anchor: لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع ، كقوله : { إن الإنسان

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r5.claim: Human means humankind generally; all people were created from a clot after the drop of semen.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r5.anchor: يريد بالإنسان جنس الناس كلهم , خلقوا من علق بعد النطفة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r6.claim: A clot is a moist piece of blood, named because its moisture makes it cling to whatever it passes; once dry it is no longer a clot.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r6.anchor: والعلقة قطعة من دم رطب سميت بذلك لأنها تعلق لرطوبتها بما تمر عليه , فإذا جفت لم تكن علقة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses the term clot in describing someone falling and spitting out the vein's blood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r7.anchor: تركناه يخر على يديه … يمج عليهما علق الوتين

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r8.claim: One purpose is to show God's favor: He formed a human from a clot until the person became upright, rational, and distinct.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r8.anchor: أحدهما : أن يبين قدر نعمته على الإنسان بأن خلقه من علقة مهيئة حتى صار بشرا سويا وعاقلا متميزا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r9.claim: A second possible purpose compares human development from stage to stage with the Prophet's passage from ignorance to completed prophethood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p304/r9.anchor: الثاني : أنه كما نقل الإنسان من حال إلى حال حتى استكمل , كذلك نقلك من الجهالة إلى النبوة حتى تستكمل محلها .

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r1.claim: Humanity is singled out from all created things because of its nobility and because revelation is directed to it; alternatively, the initially vague “created” is explained afterward to magnify human creation and its wondrous nature.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r1.anchor: تخصيص للانسان بالذكرمن بين ما يتناوله الخلق لشرفه ولأن التنزيل إليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r2.claim: The plural “clots” is used instead of the singular because the word “human” has a collective sense.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p348#5/r2.anchor: وإنما جمع ولم يقل من علقه لأن الانسان فى معنى الجمع

NAHHAS:v5p261/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p261/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p261/r6.claim: Al-insān can mean a collective; ʿalaq is its plural form from ʿalaqah.
NAHHAS:v5p261/r6.anchor: الإنسان بمعنى جماعة فلذلك قال علق وهو جمع علقة

QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r1.claim: The human is Adam's descendant; alaq is a clot or congealed blood, distinct from blood that flows, and the plural reflects humanity as a collective created from clots after sperm.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { خلق الإنسان } يعني ابن آدم. { من علق } أي من دم جمع علقة،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r2.claim: A clot is a moist piece of blood named for sticking to things it passes; when dried, it is no longer called a clot.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r2.anchor: والعلقة: قطعة من دم رطب، سميت بذلك لأنها تعلق لرطوبتها بما تمر عليه،

QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r3.claim: The poet's line about blood of the aorta dripping onto hands illustrates the word alaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: تركناه يخر على يديه يمج عليهما علق الوتين

QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r4.claim: Humanity is singled out to honor it, and to show the blessing of making a rational, fully formed human from a lowly clot.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:2/r4.anchor: وخص الإنسان بالذكر تشريفا له. وقيل: أراد أن يبين قدر نعمته عليه،

QUTB-ZILAL:96:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:2/r1.claim: The human being begins as a small, simple-formed, fixed blood point clinging to the womb.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:2/r1.anchor: من تلك النقطة الدموية الجامدة العالقة بالرحم . من ذلك المنشأ الصغير الساذج التكوين

RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r1.claim: Three grammatical readings are offered: 'created' may have no object, asserting God alone creates; an unqualified object may mean everything, with humans singled out for honor or because revelation addresses them; or the next phrase explains the initially general creation to magnify humanity.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r1.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون قوله : { الذى خلق } لا يقدر له مفعول ، ويكون المعنى أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r2.claim: The theologians argue that creation uniquely distinguishes God's essence and cannot be shared, making the power to originate the mark of divinity; prophets identify God as creator, not idols fashioned by people.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r2.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بهذه الآية على أنه لا خالق غير الله تعالى ، قالوا : لأنه سبحانه جعل الخالقية صفة مميزة لذات الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r3.claim: The verse gradually leads idolaters to acknowledge God: they admit He created them, unlike idols they carved, then concede that creator and noncreator cannot be equal.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r3.anchor: لكن اذكر لهم أنهم هم الذين خلقوا من العلقة فلا يمكنهم إنكاره ، ثم قل : ولا بد للفعل من فاعل

RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r4.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r4.claim: Theologians agree the first obligation is knowing God, considering how to know Him, or resolving to undertake that inquiry, according to their well-known disagreement.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r4.anchor: اتفق المتكلمون على أن أول الواجبات معرفة الله تعالى ، أو النظر في معرفة الله أو القصد إلى ذلك النظر

RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r5.claim: The argument also rules out natural causation: a created influence requires another cause, while an eternal cause must be either necessitated or voluntary; ordered, beneficial change indicates a knowing agent with choice.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16/r5.anchor: ودلت الآية على أن القول بالطبع باطل ، لأن المؤثر فيه إن كان حادثا افتقر إلى مؤثر آخر

RAZI-FULL:v32p16#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p16#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p16#2/r1.claim: The plural 'clinging clots' follows the generic, collective sense of 'human,' as in the statement that humanity is in loss.
RAZI-FULL:v32p16#2/r1.anchor: إنما قال : { من علق } على الجمع لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع

RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.claim: Humanity rises from the lowly clot to knowledge of realities, proving a wise governor guides this change; knowledge is the noblest human trait and God's greatest gift.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17/r7.anchor: أول حوال الإنسان كونه علقة وهي أخس الأشياء وآخر أمره هو صيرورته عالما بحقائق الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.claim: Creation of the clot-grown human provides rational proof of power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy; teaching by the pen points to revealed rulings known through transmission, so knowledge of lordship precedes and grounds prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v32p17#2/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة

SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r1.claim: Humanity is specified from among all creation because revelation is addressed to it; al-insān is generic, and alaq is plural because each person comes from a clot.
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r1.anchor: تخصيص له بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق

SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r2.claim: The repeated khalaqa may be verbal emphasis of the relative clause alone, as in a construction like the one who came, came Zayd.
SAMIN-DURR:96:2/r2.anchor: فيكون قد أكد الصلة وحدها، كقولك:

STUDYQURAN:96:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r4.claim: The blood clot appears as gestation's third stage in the Quran's fullest account, followed by a lump of flesh and further stages.
STUDYQURAN:96:1/r4.anchor: The blood clot appears to be the third stage in the most extensive Quranic account of gestation

TAB:96:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:2/r1.speaker: author
TAB:96:2/r1.claim: God created the human being from blood, expressed with the plural ʿalaq although the phrase speaks of humanity generically in the singular.
TAB:96:2/r1.anchor: خَلَقَ الإنْسانَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ يعني :  من الدم ،   وقال :  من علق والمراد به من علقة

TAB:96:2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:2/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:2/r2.claim: The singular human is treated as a collective, as in the Arabic pairings shajara/shajar and qasaba/qasab, hence ʿalaqa/ʿalaq.
TAB:96:2/r2.anchor: كما يقال :  شجرة وشجر ،   وقصَبة وقَصَب ،   وكذلك علقة وعَلَق .   وإنما قال :  من عَلَق

TAB:96:3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r4.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r4.claim: Aisha recounts true dreams, Muhammad's retreat at Hira, Gabriel's arrival and repeated command to read, and identifies these opening verses as the first revelation.
TAB:96:3/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أنها قالت :  كان أوّل ما ابتدىء به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة

TAB:96:3/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r5.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r5.claim: In Aisha's report, Khadija reassures Muhammad by citing his virtues; Waraqa identifies the revelation as Moses' angel, predicts opposition, and vows support if alive.
TAB:96:3/r5.anchor: فَقَالَتْ :  أبْشِرْ ،   فَوَاللّهِ لا يُخْزيكَ اللّهُ أبَدا ،   وَوَاللّهِ إنّكَ لَتَصِلُ الرّحَمِ

TAB:96:3/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r6.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r6.claim: Aisha's account says that after Iqra the next revelations included Nun, the Pen, al-Muddaththir, and al-Duha.
TAB:96:3/r6.anchor: ثُمّ كانَ أوّلُ ما نَزَلَ عَليّ مِنَ القُرآنِ بَعْدَ «اقْرأْ » :  ( ن والقَلَمِ وَما يَسْطُرُونَ

TAB:96:3/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
TAB:96:3/r7.claim: Ibn Shaddad reports Gabriel's reading of the opening passage, Khadija's reassurance and referral to Waraqa, then delayed revelation and al-Duha's reassurance.
TAB:96:3/r7.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن شدّاد ،   قال :  أتى جبريل محمدا ،   فقال :  يا محمد اقرأ

TAB:96:3/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r8.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r8.claim: Aisha, through ʿUrwa and al-Zuhri, is cited as saying the first thing revealed was ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created.’
TAB:96:3/r8.anchor: عن عائشة قال إبراهيم :  قال سفيان :  حفظه لنا ابن إسحاق :  إن أوّل شيء أُنزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r9.speaker: عائشة
TAB:96:3/r9.claim: A further report from Aisha says the first surah revealed was Iqra bi-smi rabbika.
TAB:96:3/r9.anchor: عن عائشة ،   أنّ أوّل سورة أُنزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r10.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB:96:3/r10.claim: ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr says the first surah sent down to the Messenger was Iqra bi-smi rabbika alladhi khalaq.
TAB:96:3/r10.anchor: عن عُبيد بن عُمير ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اقرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r11.speaker: أبو رجاء العطاردي
TAB:96:3/r11.claim: Abu Raja says he learned Iqra from Abu Musa al-Ashʿari and identifies it as Muhammad's first revealed surah.
TAB:96:3/r11.anchor: أبو رجاء العُطارديّ ،   قال :  كنا في المسجد الجامع ،   ومقرئنا أبو موسى الأشعريّ

TAB:96:3/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r12.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
TAB:96:3/r12.claim: ʿAta ibn Yasar says Iqra was the first surah revealed from the Qur'an.
TAB:96:3/r12.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ،   قال :  أوّل سورة نزلت من القرآن اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ

TAB:96:3/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:3/r13.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:3/r13.claim: Mujahid says Iqra was the first Qur'anic revelation; one transmission adds that Nun and the Pen followed.
TAB:96:3/r13.anchor: عن مجاهد ،   قال :  أوّل ما نزل من القرآن :  اقْرأْ باسْمِ رَبّكَ وزاد ابن مهديّ :  ن والْقَلَمِ
