TABATABAI:96:1-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r3.claim: ‘Humankind’ is the human species, and ʿalaq is coagulated blood—the stage to which the womb’s fertilized drop develops.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r3.anchor: المراد جنس الإنسان المتناسل والعلق الدم المتجمد

TABATABAI:96:1-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r4.claim: The human develops by successive divine governance from a clot into a complete being of astonishing traits; this shows that God is Lord because He is creator.
TABATABAI:96:1-7/r4.anchor: فلم يتم الإنسان إنسانا ولم يكمل إلا بتدبير متعاقب منه تعالى وهو بعينه خلق بعد خلق

TABRISI:96:2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r1.claim: Alaq is the plural of a coagulated piece of blood that clings while moist and is no longer called that once dry; al-alaq also names a black leech that clings to a limb and sucks blood.
TABRISI:96:2/r1.anchor: العلق جمع علقة وهي القطعة الجامدة من الدم التي تعلق لرطوبتها بما تمر به

TABRISI:96:2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2/r9.claim: Mentioning creation of the human after the general creation is specification after generality, like naming belief in the afterlife after unseen belief; Labid's line shows that blame is broader than calling someone slow.
TABRISI:96:2/r9.anchor: بعد قوله خلق خصوص بعد عموم فهو مثل قوله

TABRISI:96:2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r10.speaker: لبيد
TABRISI:96:2/r10.claim: Labid's line illustrates that accusation of slowness is a subset of reproach, so the latter is more general.

TABRISI:96:2#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:2#2/r8.claim: God created all creatures according to wisdom and power, then singles out the human for honor among animals; humankind comes from coagulated blood after the sperm. The source prefers this over the view that Adam was made from hand-clinging clay. The lowly origin's development into balanced humanity parallels the Prophet's transformation from ignorance to prophethood.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r8.anchor: أراد به جنس بني آدم أي خلقتهم من دم جامد بعد النطفة

TABRISI:96:2#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2#2/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:96:2#2/r9.claim: A competing reading says the verse means Adam was made from clay that clings to the hand; the author says the account of humankind's origin is sounder.
TABRISI:96:2#2/r9.anchor: معناه خلق آدم من طين يعلق باليد والأول أصح

THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.claim: ʿAlaq means a clinging blood clot, its singular is ʿalaqa, and “the human” is singular in wording but collective in meaning.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r1.anchor: خلق الإنسان من علق أي الدم، واحدتها علقة، وإنما جمع ولفظ الإنسان واحد، لأنه في معنى الجمع

THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.claim: Most scholars say this was the first surah revealed, with its first five verses the first revelation.
THALABI:v10p242#3/r2.anchor: وهذه أول سورة نزلت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن، وأول ما نزل منها خمس آيات من

ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r1.claim: The past-tense creation verb indicates that divine creation is continually repeated.
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r1.anchor: the act of divine creation (khalq) has been and is being continuously repeated

ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r2.claim: The fertilized ovum origin contrasts biological simplicity with intellectual and spiritual potential, pointing to conscious design and purpose in life.
ASAD-NOTES:96:1#n2/r2.anchor: contrasting the primitiveness and simplicity of his biological origins with his intellectual and spiritual potential

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#3/r1.claim: Al-insān means Adam's descendants; ʿalaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, used collectively to match the collective meaning of humankind and the sūra's verse endings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p169#3/r1.anchor: {خلق الإنسان} يعني ابن آدم. {من علق} جمع علقه، وإنما ذكر العلق بلفظ الجمع

WAHIDI-QT:96:2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:2/r1.claim: The human means Adam's descendants, created from clots of blood.
WAHIDI-QT:96:2/r1.anchor: يعني ابن آدم { من علق } جمع علقة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r3.claim: The human being means Adam's descendant, created from clinging-clots; alaq is the plural of alaqa.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:1-8/r3.anchor: خلق الإنسان } يعني: ابن آدم { من علق } جمع علقة.

ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.claim: The third command began the Qur'an and simultaneously miraculously made the unreading Prophet able to read, fixed the text to be recited, and taught him to introduce the Creator, as related to 29:48 and 42:52.
ELMALILI:96:1-8/r3.anchor: Kur’an üçüncü defaki tazyikten sonra olan işbu ٱقْرَأْ بِٱسْمِ رَبِّكَ emriyle başlamıştı

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r7.claim: Alaq literally means something clinging or attached; it can refer to blood or a clot, the womb's attached embryo, a leech, pulley, rope, or well-used path, and also spiritual love or attachment.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r7.anchor: maddesi yapışıp ilişmek mânasına mevzû‘dur. Ve mutlaka ilişken ve yapışkan nesneye de denir.

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r8.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r8.claim: Beyzawi treats alaq as a plural of alaqa because insan is collective in meaning.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r8.anchor: Beyzâvî “insan” cemi‘[^8] mânasında olduğu için cemi‘lenmiştir der

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r9.speaker: Müfessirîn
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r9.claim: Commentators commonly take the word materially as plural embryonic clots after fertilization, emphasizing ascent from a low beginning to a higher state.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r9.anchor: Müfessirîn, halkın maddî haysiyetini nazar-ı i‘tibâra alarak

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r10.claim: Elmalılı prefers singular “attachment,” broad enough to include spiritual relation from God and every stage of human creation, and to urge loving attention to what is read.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r10.anchor: bir ilişik mânasına müfred olarak mülâhaza edilmesine

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r11.claim: On either reading, the point is that the Lord who creates a human from a clot or mere attachment can certainly teach a person who has never read to read.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r11.anchor: Bir alekadan, yahut mücerred bir ilişikten bir insan halkeden ve ale’l-ıtlâk halketmek kendinin şânı olan Rabbin hiç okumamış olanı da böyle bir emir ile elbette okutur

ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.speaker: Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.claim: Beyzawi says God recounts the human's beginning and end while moving him from the lowest state to the highest, first indicating rational knowledge of God and then signifying transmitted knowledge.
ELMALILI:96:1-8#2/r17.anchor: Beyzâvî der ki: “Allah sübhânehu insanı ehass-ı merâtibden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.claim: These were the first revelation; the command to read addresses Muhammad and all Muslims, and its repetition stresses the importance of reading and knowledge, through which humans are distinguished among living things.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r1.anchor: İlk vahyin “oku” emriyle başlaması ve bu emrin iki defa tekrar edilmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r5.claim: Alaq has dictionary senses including attachment, affection, clotted blood, or a blood-sucking worm; here it is understood as the fertilized ovum attached to the uterine wall, and knowing Creator and creation is necessary for human development.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:1/r5.anchor: aşılanmış yumurtanın ana rahminin iç cidarına asılı vaziyetinin (zigot) kastedildiği anlaşılmaktadır

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r8.claim: ʿAlaq is a collective for something sticky or attached, the embryonic stage following the sperm drop in Quranic descriptions of development.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r8.anchor: In allen diesen Stellen wird das Nomen unitatis ʿalaqa, „etwas Anhaftendes bzw. Klebriges“ (in Q 96 steht das Kollektivum ʿalaq)

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r9.claim: The opening verses describe embryonic development in the womb, not the biblical creation of Adam from earth or clay.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r9.anchor: Die beiden Anfangsverse von Sure 96 handeln also von der Entstehung des Embryos im Mutterleib

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r10.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r10.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r10.claim: Other early Meccan passages likewise call natural development in the womb God's creation, distinguishing this verse from later accounts that begin with Adam's formation from earth.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r10.anchor: zumal die natürliche Entstehung des Kindes im Mutterleib auch in weiteren frühmekkanischen Texten als eine „Erschaffung“ (ḫalaqa) durch Gott beschrieben wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r11.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r11.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r11.claim: General early Meccan statements that humans are created probably refer to embryos rather than Adam, especially in suras earlier than Q 55.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r11.anchor: Allgemeine Aussagen über die Erschaffung des Menschen wie 95:4 (la-qad ḫalaqnă l-ʾinsāna fī ʾaḥsani taqwīm)

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r12.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r12.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r12.claim: Ḫalaqa in verse 2 is a generic present expressed with a perfect form, consistent with the verb's original aspectual rather than temporal function.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r12.anchor: Die 3. Sg. Perfekt ḫalaqa dürfte deshalb als „generelles Präsens“ zu werten sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r13.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r13.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r13.claim: Aspectual perfects often occur in Quranic affirmations of God's works; early examples include the paired actions in 87:4–5 and 53:43–44.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:1-2:anmerkung/r13.anchor: Aspektuelle – also nicht bereits morphologisch auf eine Vergangenheitsbedeutung festgelegte – Perfektformen kommen insbesondere in koranischen Werkaffirmationen des öfteren vor

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r1.claim: The human creation verse specifies the general mention of creation in verse 1.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r1.anchor: This is an expression of the specific after the general.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r2.claim: ʿAlaq means a clot of congealed blood, recalling embryonic stages also discussed in al-Ḥajj, al-Muʾminūn, al-Sajdah, al-Qiyāmah, and al-Dahr.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r3.claim: Human development displays God's power and wisdom, making resurrection possible; it also shows purposeful creation that entails accountability for deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r3.anchor: He fashions out a living being having such faculties

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r4.claim: Being made from trivial material gives no grounds for pride, self-glorification, or self-veneration.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p386/r4.anchor: man who has been created from such trivial and inconsequential stuff to show conceit and pride

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r3.claim: Al-insān is generic, and ʿalaq is the plural of ʿalaqa; the verse names the creation humans acknowledge, while leaving Adam's origin aside because unbelievers do not accept it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p507/r3.anchor: والإنسان هنا اسم جنس، والعلق جمع علقة، فلذلك جاء من علق، وإنما ذكر من خلق من علق لأنهم مقرون به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.claim: The preceding surah described humanity's best form; this surah explains its material origin in clinging blood and expands on its afterlife condition, linking the two surahs thematically.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p178/r5.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة التين خلق الإنسان في أحسن تقويم بين عز وجل هنا أنه تعالى خلق الإنسان من علق

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r1.claim: Human is singled out as the noblest creation, whose remarkable design strongly demonstrates the worship implied by the reading command; repeating it may also magnify it by first leaving it indefinite.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r1.anchor: إنه أشرف المخلوقات وفيه من بدائع الصنع والتدبير ما فيه أدل على وجوب العبادة المقصودة من القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says mentioning human creation after the command to read signals that humanity was created for Quranic reading and understanding, as in the opening of al-Rahman.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r2.anchor: وعن الزمخشري أن المناسب أن يراد خلق الإنسان بعد الأمر بقراءة القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r3.claim: Clinging blood displays God's power through the sharp contrast between the human's initial and later states; the plural form matches humanity as a genus and preserves the rhyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r3.anchor: لبيان كمال قدرته تعالى بإظهار ما بين حالتيه الأولى والآخرة من التباين البين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r4.claim: One explanation for naming this stage is that sperm and earth are farther from developed humanity, although they might seem even clearer proofs of divine power.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r4.anchor: ولعله على ما قيل السر في تخصيص هذا الطور من بين سائر أطواره

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r5.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r5.claim: Al-Bahr says the verse omits Adam's original material, earth, because disbelievers were not familiar with that creation; it instead mentions the derivative material to bring the point nearer to their understanding, though al-Alusi says this does not fully answer the question.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r5.anchor: وفي البحر لم يذكر سبحانه مادة الأصل يعني آدم عليه السلام وهو التراب

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r6.claim: Another view sees a reminder of the clinging blood removed from Muhammad's chest before his mission, preparing him for revelation and linking this surah to al-Sharh, especially if that surah means literal chest-splitting.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r6.anchor: وقيل خص هذا الطور تذكيرا له عليه الصلاة والسلام لما وقع من شرح الصدر قبل النبوة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r7.claim: The claim that human here means Adam created from something that clings to the hand is unacceptable to al-Alusi.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p180/r7.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن المراد بالإنسان آدم عليه السلام وإن المعنى خلق آدم من طبق يعلق باليد وهو مما لا تعلق به يد القبول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.claim: Most commentators say this was the first sura revealed and that its first five verses, through the words about what humanity did not know, were the first revelation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين: على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات من أولها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.claim: Aisha says revelation began with true dreams and retreat to Hira; Gabriel commanded the Prophet to read and squeezed him three times before reciting these verses; he returned frightened and Khadija reassured him through his virtues.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.claim: Khadija brought the Prophet to Waraqa, who identified the visitor as the messenger sent to Moses, predicted his people would expel him, and promised support before dying as revelation paused.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p474#2/r3.anchor: فانطلقت به خديجة حتى أتت به ورقة بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r2.claim: Alaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a clinging clot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p479/r2.anchor: من علق} جمع علقة. {اقرأ} كرره تأكيدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r3.claim: The human being created from a clot is first left unspecified and then explained to magnify the creation's marvel; علق is plural by agreement with الإنسان in collective meaning.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r3.anchor: فأبهم أولا ثم فسر تفخيما لخلقه ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.claim: Since knowing God is the first obligation, the opening verses first show His existence, immense power, and complete wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:1-3/r4.anchor: ولما كان أول الواجبات معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى نزل أولا ما يدل على وجوده

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.claim: God recounts humanity's beginning and destination to show the favor of raising it from the lowest rank to the highest, affirm His lordship and generosity, and move from rational proof to sensory evidence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:4-8/r3.anchor: وقد عدد سبحانه وتعالى مبدأ أمر الإنسان ومنتهاه إظهارا لما أنعم عليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.claim: She presents the surah’s opening as the first revelation, noting that Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report no disagreement about that account.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r2.anchor: والمشهور كذلك أنه أمل سورة نزلت من الوحي. ولم يشر "ابن إسحاق" في (السيرة النبوية) إلي خلاف

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.claim: Aisha recounts Muhammad’s true dreams, retreat to Hira, Gabriel’s command and three embraces, and the recitation of the opening five verses, which remained fixed in his heart; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r3.anchor: عن "السيدة عائشة أم المؤمنين" قالت: "كان أول ما ابتدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي

BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.claim: Aisha continues that Muhammad saw Gabriel in the sky, returned to Khadija, and was reassured because his character included kinship, truthfulness, trustworthiness, hospitality, and helping in adversity; no grading is stated.
BINTSHATI:v2p13/r4.anchor: فقالت: أبشر يا ابن عم واثبت، فوالله لا يخزيك الله أبداً، إنك لتصل الرحم وتصدق الحديث

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.claim: Al-Razi also transmits that only al-Alaq’s first five verses came at the start; the remainder came after public opposition and were joined to the surah by God’s command.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r3.anchor: أن الذي نزل من السورة أول الوحي، آياتها الخمس الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.claim: Al-Bahr al-Muhit says the surah is Meccan and its opening was the first revelation at Hira, as established in Bukhari and elsewhere; it judges the claims that al-Muddaththir or the Fatiha came first unsound.
BINTSHATI:v2p14/r4.anchor: وقول جابر: أول ما نزل المدثر، وقول أبي ميسرة عمرو بن شرحبيل: أول ما نزل الفاتحة، لا يصح

BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.claim: The reports in al-Tabari and the Prophetic biography stop the first-revelation account at verse five, supporting the view that the opening alone was first revealed.
BINTSHATI:v2p15/r1.anchor: حيث يقف الحديث فيهما عن اول ما نزل من الوحي، عند الآية الخامسة

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.claim: The first verse states creation generally, while the next specifies the human, recipient of revelation and the one uniquely able to read, learn, and bear religious responsibility.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r1.anchor: تخصيص هذا العام، باللفت إلى خلق الإنسان، من حيث كان الوحي القرآني لهداية هذا الإنسان

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r4.speaker: بعض السلف
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r4.claim: Some early authorities read the human’s creation from a clot as reassurance that the Lord who summoned and nurtured Muhammad had cared for him from that earliest stage.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r4.anchor: من السلف من تأويله على أن المقصود به إيناس الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى ربه الذي دعاه ورباه

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r5.speaker: آخرون من السلف
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r5.claim: Other early authorities take the mention of the clot as a gradual argument bringing idolaters to acknowledge their Creator, as in al-Razi’s account.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r5.anchor: وآخرون منهم تأولوه على قصد التدرج بعباد الأوثان إلى الإقرار بخالفتهم

BINTSHATI:v2p17/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the verse magnifies human creation and displays its remarkable constitution; al-Razi adds that moving from lowly clot to noble knowledge requires a directing Maker.
BINTSHATI:v2p17/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري إن في الآية تفخيماً لخلق الإنسان ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan says Rabbuka comforts Muhammad and identifies his exclusive Lord; the Creator attribute follows because Arabs called idols lords, though idols cannot create.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r1.anchor: ذكر {رَبَّكُ} في الآية الأولى، إيناس للمصطفى وتعيين لربه، لا رب غيره

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r2.claim: She rejects modern embryology as the verse’s intended lesson: its first audience had no conception of that science, and the Quran would not offer an unintelligible sign.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r2.anchor: وغير متصور أن يكون القرآن الكريم قدم لهم من آيات ربوبية الخالق وقدرته، ما لا سبيل لأحد منهم إلى تصوره

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r3.claim: In Arabic, علق can mean material things that cling or adhere, such as blood, and figuratively an attachment or bond of love or hatred.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r3.anchor: والعربية قد استعملت العلق مادياً في كل ما يعلق وينشب: كالدم

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r4.claim: The familiar expression علقت المرأة means that a woman became pregnant; علق here is the plural of علقة and preserves the generic scope of الإنسان.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r4.anchor: وهم الذين ألفوا استعمال: علقت المرآة، بمعنى حملت. واستعمال العلق هنا، جمع علقة

BINTSHATI:v2p18/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r5.claim: The verse is a sign of human creation, knowledge, and moral responsibility, followed by the human’s delusion of independence and forgetfulness of return to God.
BINTSHATI:v2p18/r5.anchor: وإنما هي آية الله في هذا الإنسان، خلقه من علق، وخصه بالعلم، واحتمل أمانة التكليف

BINTSHATI:v2p19/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r1.claim: The first revelation briefly sketches humanity’s whole story from origin to end, a sketch expanded in later revelations.
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r1.anchor: وهذه هي قصة الإنسان، من المبدأ إلى المنتهى، تلفت إليه سورة الوحي الأولى، بإيجاز

BINTSHATI:v2p19/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r2.claim: Passages revealed later trace humanity from creation through death and resurrection, linking human origins to accountability and return.
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r2.anchor: هذا الإنسان الذي خلق الله من علق، وعلمه ما لم يكن يعلم، وإليه رجعاع

BINTSHATI:v2p19/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r3.claim: These creation passages do not direct readers to embryology; they argue that the Creator can raise people again for judgment, reward, punishment, and religious responsibility.
BINTSHATI:v2p19/r3.anchor: وما من آية فيها، يؤذن سياقها بتوجيه إلى النظر في علم الأجنة وعلم الأحياء والتشريح

BINTSHATI:v2p26/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r1.claim: The return to God is linked to human creation from a clot: God is both the beginning and the end, as also stated in Surat al-Layl.
BINTSHATI:v2p26/r1.anchor: ارتباطهما بخلق الإنسان من علق، إيذاناً بأن إليه تعالى المبتدأ والمنتهى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r3.claim: A person who knows he was created from clinging blood can infer that his Creator can resurrect him from dust, which is more receptive to life than blood; belief in resurrection should prompt action.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r3.anchor: فإن التراب أقبل للحياة من الدم ، ومن صدق بالإعادة عمل لها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r4.claim: The clinging substance is singled out as the carrier of life, which is why it is called a soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p478#s096/r4.anchor: وخص العلق لأنه مركب الحياة ، ولذلك سمي نفسا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r4.claim: Humanity is singled out because humans are the highest animals and a concentrated summary of creation, making their creation an especially clear proof of the Maker and the duty to worship Him alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r4.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكمل الحيوان وزبدة مخضه , ولباب حقيقته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r5.claim: The word al-ʿalaq denotes thick, deep-red clotted blood and can also denote sticky clay; Arabs acknowledged both as origins of human creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r5.anchor: أي خلق هذا النوع من هذا الشيء وهو دم شديد الحمرة جامد غليظ

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r6.claim: Blood is the source and carrier of life, and the verse presents creation through causes even though God can create without a causal sequence; the author also says eating blood imparts its qualities.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r6.anchor: لأنه أصل الإنسان وغيره من الحيوان وهو مركب الحياة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r7.claim: The shared word al-ʿalaq supports the Shāfiʿī proof for using a homonym with both meanings at once; its breadth may encompass clay as well as blood.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r7.anchor: فالآية من أدلة إمامنا الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على استعمال المشترك في معنييه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r8.claim: The verse implies that blood and earth are unlawful as food in their original states but become lawful after transformation; reddish semen is not transformed, while blood turned to flesh and earth mixed with water into grain or dates are transformed.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p479/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى حرمة أكل ما هو أصلنا من الدم والتراب قبل أن يستحيل

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r1.claim: The author classifies the chapter as Meccan and counts nineteen verses.

DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.claim: Aisha's account describes true dreams and retreat at Hira before Gabriel commands him to read, presses him three times, and recites the first five verses; Muhammad returns trembling to Khadija.
DURR-FULL:v8p560/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم

TAB:96:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:1/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:1/r2.claim: The adjacent verse says humanity was created from blood; ‘alaq’ is plural in form while referring to one clot.
TAB:96:1/r2.anchor: خلق الإنسان من علق يعني :  من الدم

TAB:96:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:1/r3.speaker: author
TAB:96:1/r3.claim: The plural pattern follows ordinary pairs such as tree/trees and reed/reeds; ‘human’ is singular in wording but collective in sense, so ‘clots’ is used.
TAB:96:1/r3.anchor: لأنه ذهب إلى الجمع ،   كما يقال :  شجرة وشجر ،   وقصبة وقصب

BURHAN:v2p470/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.claim: The command first states that God created generally, then singles out the human being's creation from a clot.
BURHAN:v2p470/r2.anchor: وقوله ﴿ اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق ﴾ فعم بقوله ﴿ خلق ﴾ جميع مخلوقاته ثم خص فقال

BURHAN:v1p407#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r1.claim: Omitting the final nūn of the verb marks a small or humble starting point from which creation develops toward what only God can encompass; the human begins as a despised drop.
BURHAN:v1p407#2/r1.anchor: حذفت النون تنبيها على مهانة مبتدأ الإنسان وصغر قدره بحسب ما يدرك هو من نفسه

ITQAN:v3p284/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.claim: The opening of “Read” similarly previews the Qur’an: it commands reading, begins in God’s name, signals legal knowledge and the principles of religion, and reports God’s teaching of what humans did not know; it can therefore be called the Qur’an’s title.
ITQAN:v3p284/r3.anchor: وكذلك أول سورة ( اقرأ فإنها مشتملة على نظير ما اشتملت عليه الفاتحة من براعة الاستهلال

ITQAN:v3p196/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.claim: Repeating al-insan creates paronomasia: the first is humanity as a species, the second may be Adam, a literate person, or Idris, and the third is Abu Jahl.
ITQAN:v3p196/r1.anchor: ومثله ابن الصائغ بقوله ﴿ خلق الإنسان من علق ﴾ ثم قال ﴿ علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم كلا إن الإنسان ليطغى

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.speaker: عائشة رضي الله عنها
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha says revelation began with true dreams and seclusion at Ḥirāʾ; Gabriel's repeated commands to recite introduced al-ʿAlaq, and the shaken Prophet was comforted by Khadīja, who cited his virtues. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p10/r1.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: "أول ما بدئ به رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من الوحي الرؤيا الصادقة في النوم

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.speaker: بعض علمائهم
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.claim: Ibn Shihāb relays from Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād that some scholars said al-ʿAlaq's first five verses were revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the remainder came later as God willed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p11/r2.anchor: أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول: كان أول ما أنزل الله على رسوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - {اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r1.claim: Bint al-Shati reads the opening command to read together with the signs of human creation from a clot, writing by the pen, and the teaching of what was unknown.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r1.anchor: وفيها لفت إلى آية الله الكبرى في الإنسان، خلقه الله من علق، وعلم بالقلم، علم الإنسان ما لم يعلم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r2.claim: The isolated nūn opening Sūrat al-Qalam points to the letter as a basis of reading, knowledge, and expression: alone it gives only sound, but in a word its deeper significance emerges.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r2.anchor: منفردا منقطعا فلا يعطي أي معنى أو دلالة، وما يخرج عن مجرد صوت. ثم يأخذ الحرف موضعه من الكلمة فيتجلى سره الأكبر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r3.claim: The Prophet had not read or copied scripture before the Quran, and the pagans knew it was not the familiar tales they wrote down, yet resisted believing in a human messenger.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r3.anchor: وما كان المصطفى بقارئ، ولا كان يتلو من كتاب من قبل القرآن ولا يخطه بيمينه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r4.claim: The Quran first confronts its opponents through the wonder of its eloquence; when they persist in defiance, it turns to an explicit challenge that compels them with proof.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r4.anchor: فلما أصروا على عنادهم، اتجه إلى صريح التحدي والمعاجزة، إلزاما لهم بالحجة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r5.claim: Before the explicit challenge, nine Meccan suras opened with disjointed letters amid accusations of folklore, poetry, soothsaying, and magic; their rebuttals console the Prophet and recall punished earlier peoples.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p162/r5.anchor: وقيبل التحدي والمعاجزة، في العهد المكي، نزلت تسع سور مفتتحة بالحروف المقطعة

IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.speaker: عبيد
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.claim: Ubayd's report says Muhammad annually secluded himself at Hira during Ramadan, fed the poor, and returned to circumambulate the Kaaba; Gabriel then came with a written silk cloth and commanded him to recite, repeating the embrace three times, after which Muhammad woke with the words fixed in his heart.
IBNHISHAM:v1p235#2/r3.anchor: قال عبيد: فكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجاور ذلك الشهر من كل سنة، يطعم من جاءه من المساكين

ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r1.claim: The human is singled out among creatures as the recipient of revelation and as the most honored; Abū Ḥayyān notes al-Zamakhshari's suggestion that this implies angels are more honored.
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r1.anchor: وخصه من بين المخلوقات لكونه هو المنزل إليه ، وهو أشرف . قال الزمخشري : أشرف ما على الأرض

ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows the relative phrase who created to be left general and then explained by خلق الإنسان, magnifying human creation and its wondrous constitution.
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r2.anchor:
قال الزمخشري : أشرف ما على الأرض ، وفيه دسيسة أن الملك أشرف .
وقال : ويجوز أن يراد الذي خلق الإنسان

ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r3.claim: الإنسان is generic, and علق is the plural of علقة, accounting for the form من علق.
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r3.anchor: والإنسان هنا اسم جنس ، والعلق جمع علقة ، فلذلك جاء من علق

ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r4.claim: The verse mentions creation from a clot because the hearers acknowledged it; Adam as the origin is omitted because disbelievers did not accept it as established.
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر من خلق من علق لأنهم مقرون به ، ولم يذكر أصلهم آدم ، لأنه ليس متقرراً عند الكفار

ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r5.claim: The argument starts with the human descendant, which was accessible to their understanding, and omits the original creation to bring the point closer to them.
ABUHAYYAN:96:2/r5.anchor: لأنه ليس متقرراً عند الكفار فيسبق الفرع ، وترك أصل الخلقة تقريباً لأفهامهم

ALUSI:96:2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r1.claim: The human is the noblest creature, whose wondrous design makes him especially strong evidence for the duty of worship commanded with recitation.
ALUSI:96:2/r1.anchor: إنه أشرف المخلوقات وفيه من بدائع الصنع والتدبير ما فيه فهو أدل على وجوب العبادة المقصودة من القراءة

ALUSI:96:2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r2.claim: The human may be left unnamed at first and identified afterward, magnifying him through initial ambiguity followed by explanation.
ALUSI:96:2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد خلق الإنسان إلا أنه لم يذكر أولاً وذكر ثانياً قصداً لتفخيمه بالإبهام ثم التفسير

ALUSI:96:2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI:96:2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says human creation after the command to recite the Qur’an signals that humanity was created for recitation and understanding, as in the opening of al-Raḥmān.
ALUSI:96:2/r3.anchor: وعن الزمخشري أن المناسب أن يراد خلق الإنسان بعد الأمر بقرارة القرآن تنبيهاً على أنه تعالى خلقه للقراءة والدراية

ALUSI:96:2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r4.claim: ʿAlaq means clotted blood; this stage displays God’s power through the striking difference between the human’s first and final states.
ALUSI:96:2/r4.anchor: أي دم جامد لبيان كمال قدرته تعالى بإظهار ما بين حالتيه الأولى والآخرة من التباين البين

ALUSI:96:2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r5.claim: Because al-insān denotes humanity as a generic collective, ʿalaq is plural to match it; the form also preserves the verse endings.
ALUSI:96:2/r5.anchor: لأن الإنسان مراد به الجنس فهو في معنى الجمع فأتى بما خلق منه كذلك ليطابقه مع ما في ذلك من رعاية الفواصل

ALUSI:96:2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r6.claim: A proposed reason for singling out the ʿalaq stage is that it is closer to humanity than the sperm-drop or soil, though those stages more clearly show divine power.
ALUSI:96:2/r6.anchor: ولعله على ما قيل السر في تخصيص هذا الطور من بين سائر أطوار الفطرة الإنسانية مع كون النطفة والترب أدل على كمال القدرة

ALUSI:96:2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r7.speaker: البحر
ALUSI:96:2/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr says the verse names the descendant’s material rather than Adam’s soil because unbelievers did not know Adam’s creation from soil; this eases their understanding but leaves the question unresolved.
ALUSI:96:2/r7.anchor: وفي «البحر » لم يذكر سبحانه مادة الأصل يعني آدم عليه السلام وهو التراب لأن خلقه من ذلك لم يكن متقرراً عند الكفار

ALUSI:96:2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:96:2/r8.claim: Another explanation links the chosen stage to the pre-prophetic opening of the Prophet’s chest and its preparation for revelation, strengthening the link with al-Sharḥ, especially if its opening is read as chest-splitting.
ALUSI:96:2/r8.anchor: وقيل خص هذا الطور تذكيراً له عليه الصلاة والسلام لما وقع من شرح الصدر قبل النبوة وإخراج العلق منه

ALUSI:96:2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r9.speaker: بعض الناس
ALUSI:96:2/r9.claim: Some take al-insān here as Adam, created from hand-sticking clay; al-Ālūsī rejects this as unacceptable.
ALUSI:96:2/r9.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أن المراد بالإنسان آدم عليه السلام وأن المعنى خلق آدم من طين يعلق باليد وهو مما لا تعلق به يد القبول

ALUSI:96:2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:2/r10.claim: Human creation is the first bestowed blessing and earliest proof of God’s existence and attributes, so it is cited to show His power to enable the Prophet to recite.
ALUSI:96:2/r10.anchor: ولما كان خلق الإنسان أول النعم الفائضة عليه منه تعالى وأقدم الدلائل الدالة على وجوده عز وجل وكمال قدرته وعلمه وحكمته سبحانه

BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.claim: Most commentators hold that this was the first sūra revealed and that the first revelation was its opening five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r2.anchor: أكثر المفسرين : على أن هذه السورة أول سورة نزلت من القرآن ، وأول ما نزل خمس آيات

BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.claim: Aisha recounts the Prophet’s true dreams, retreat and worship at Hira, then Gabriel’s command to read and three forceful embraces before reciting the opening revelation; Baghawi gives no grading.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r3.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : " أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.claim: After the revelation the frightened Prophet returned to Khadija, who reassured him that God would never disgrace him because he maintained kinship, supported the needy, hosted guests, and aided people in hardship.
BAGHAWI:96:1/r4.anchor: فقالت خديجة : كلا ، والله ما يخزيك الله أبداً ، إنك لتصل الرحم ، وتحمل الكل ، وتكسب المعدوم

BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.claim: In a Bukhari version, al-Zuhri adds that revelation paused and the Prophet, in grief, repeatedly approached mountain peaks intending to throw himself down until Gabriel reassured him; the addition is introduced as “what reached us.”
BAGHAWI:96:1/r6.anchor: حتى حزن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما بلغنا حزناً غدا منه مراراً حتى يتردى من رؤوس شواهق الجبال

BAGHAWI:96:2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:2/r1.claim: The human created is Adam’s descendant, the human being.

BAGHAWI:96:2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:2/r2.claim: ʿAlaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a clinging clot.

BAYDAWI:96:2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:2/r1.claim: The human is singled out as the noblest and clearest work of creation, and as evidence for the worship commanded by recitation.
BAYDAWI:96:2/r1.anchor: ثم أفرد ما هو أشرف وأظهر صنعا وتدبيرا

BAYDAWI:96:2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:2/r2.claim: The phrase either begins a new statement about creating the human or completes the relative description of the creator.
BAYDAWI:96:2/r2.anchor: خلق الإنسان أو الذي خلق الإنسان

BAYDAWI:96:2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:2/r3.claim: The human is first left unspecified, then named to magnify the creation and draw attention to its wondrous constitution.
BAYDAWI:96:2/r3.anchor: تفخيما لخلقه ، ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

BAYDAWI:96:2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:2/r4.claim: The plural ʿalaq is used with al-insān as a collective noun.
BAYDAWI:96:2/r4.anchor: جمعه على الإنسان في معنى الجمع

BIQAI:96:2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r1.claim: Humans are singled out because man is the highest animal and the essence of its kind, gathers the qualities of the cosmos, and is especially wondrous to create, proving the Maker's perfection and exclusive right to worship.
BIQAI:96:2/r1.anchor: وكان الإنسان أكمل الحيوان وزبدة مخضه

BIQAI:96:2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r2.claim: Al-insān here is the human species, characterized by familiarity with itself, its sensed traits, and the people of its own kind.
BIQAI:96:2/r2.anchor: أي هذا الجنس الذي من شأنه الأنس بنفسه وما رأى من أخلاقه وحسه

BIQAI:96:2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r3.claim: Blood is the origin of humans and other animals and the substance of life; God forbade eating it because it imparts its own nature to the eater.
BIQAI:96:2/r3.anchor: وكان الله تعالى قد حرمه لأنه أصل الإنسان وغيره من الحيوان

BIQAI:96:2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r4.claim: God built this world on causal processes and wisdom, although He can create directly without a chain of causes.
BIQAI:96:2/r4.anchor: بنى هذه الدار على حكمة الأسباب مع قدرته على الإيجاد من غير تطوير في تسبيب

BIQAI:96:2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r5.claim: ʿAlaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a thick, dark-red clotted blood; the same term also names mud that sticks to the hand.
BIQAI:96:2/r5.anchor: وهو دم شديد الحمرة جامد غليظ

BIQAI:96:2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r6.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI:96:2/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī uses this verse as evidence that a shared term may be applied to both of its meanings at once, since human creation is associated with both blood and sticky earth.
BIQAI:96:2/r6.anchor: فالآية من أدلة إمامنا الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على استعمال المشترك في معنييه

BIQAI:96:2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r7.claim: The wording may also allude to the prohibition of eating our original substances, blood and earth, before transformation; once they transform, they may become lawful, since transformation affects legal status in marriage and other matters.
BIQAI:96:2/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى حرمة أكل ما هو أصلنا من الدم والتراب قبل أن يستحيل

BIQAI:96:2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r8.claim: A red emission of semen is not a transformation, since it was already red before desire reduced it; sometimes desire is too weak to condense it and it is emitted red.

BIQAI:96:2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:2/r9.claim: Blood that transforms into flesh takes the ruling of lawful flesh, as earth mixed with water and transformed into dates or grain becomes lawful.
BIQAI:96:2/r9.anchor: فإذا تحول الدم لحماً صار إلى جنس ما يحل

BIQAI:96:2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r10.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the question about what could make the Prophet disbelieve in judgment cannot imply his own doubt; its intended audience is his community, who may hesitate despite clear evidence.
BIQAI:96:2/r10.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما قال الله سبحانه وتعالى لنبيه

BIQAI:96:2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr compares the address to conditional warnings such as the threat that associating partners would void one's works: its wording can extend to the Prophet, while its actual concern is the community, who are not protected from error.
BIQAI:96:2/r11.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r12.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr argues that, since God is the wisest judge, differences among people after their creation in the best form cannot be purposeless; creation is not vain.
BIQAI:96:2/r12.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r13.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr connects the placement of al-ʿAlaq after al-Tīn to the Qurʾān as the remedy that explains beginnings and ends; recitation and reflection clarify the way, and the Qurʾān is guidance, mercy, and good news.
BIQAI:96:2/r13.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r14.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links humanity's creation in the best form and return to the lowest state to divergence in people's destinies and views, all according to prior wisdom and will; God could have given every soul its guidance.
BIQAI:96:2/r14.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r15.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r15.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the two preceding sūras describe the highest human destiny, the Prophet's promised satisfaction and the excellence of his state, surpassing even Moses' prayer for an expanded breast.
BIQAI:96:2/r15.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r16.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r16.claim: Al-ʿAlaq then points to the other end of the human spectrum, from the one who forbids a servant to pray through the command not to obey him, contrasting the two ranks.
BIQAI:96:2/r16.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

BIQAI:96:2/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:2/r17.speaker: أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:96:2/r17.claim: Answering the objection that al-ʿAlaq was among the earliest revelations, Ibn al-Zubayr says sūra order follows the Prophet's arrangement, whether divinely instructed or based on the Companions' judgment, not chronology.
BIQAI:96:2/r17.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير

DURR:96:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r3.speaker: بعض علمائهم
DURR:96:1/r3.claim: Scholars heard by Muḥammad b. ʿAbbād said the opening through 96:5 was revealed at Ḥirāʾ; the sūra’s ending came later as God willed.
DURR:96:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن شهاب : حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر المخزومي أنه سمع بعض علمائهم يقول

DURR:96:1/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r6.claim: In ʿĀʾisha’s account, Gabriel commanded the unlettered Prophet to recite, squeezed him three times, then delivered the opening five verses at Ḥirāʾ.
DURR:96:1/r6.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت : «أول ما بدئ به رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة

DURR:96:1/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first revelation consisted of five verses, ending with “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أول شيء أنزل من القرآن خمس آيات { اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق } إلى قوله : { ما لم يعلم } .

DURR:96:1/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r15.speaker: الزهري وعمرو بن دينار
DURR:96:1/r15.claim: Al-Zuhrī and ʿAmr b. Dīnār report that, at Ḥirāʾ, an angel brought the Prophet brocade bearing the opening five verses in writing.
DURR:96:1/r15.anchor: عن الزهري وعمرو بن دينار أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذا أتاه ملك بنمط من ديباج

DURR:96:1/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r16.speaker: عمرو بن جابر
DURR:96:1/r16.claim: ʿAmr b. Jābir likewise reports that an angel came to the Prophet at Ḥirāʾ with brocade inscribed through “what he did not know.”
DURR:96:1/r16.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان بحراء إذ أتاه ملك

DURR:96:1/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r17.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
DURR:96:1/r17.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Shaddād recounts Gabriel’s repeated command to recite and squeezing of Muhammad, who then received the opening passage through 96:5.
DURR:96:1/r17.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شداد قال : «أتى جبريل محمداً صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : يا محمد اقرأ

DURR:96:1/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:1/r19.speaker: عائشة
DURR:96:1/r19.claim: A second ʿĀʾisha account describes Gabriel’s vast appearance, washing the Prophet’s opened chest, teaching the opening five verses, and weighing him against men; Michael says his community will follow.
DURR:96:1/r19.anchor: عن عائشة «أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم اعتكف هو وخديجة شهراً فوافق ذلك رمضان

IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.speaker: عائشة، أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.claim: Sound reports from Aisha establish that these first five verses were first, delivered to Muhammad in Hira on Ramadan 17, year 40 after the Elephant; Abu Musa and most exegetes agree.
IBNASHUR:96:1/r7.anchor: وهي أول سورة نزلت في القرآن كما ثبت في الأحاديث الصحيحة الواضحة ، ونزل أولها بغار حراء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:1/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:1/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:1/r13.claim: The surah directs him to reflect on God's creation, especially the astonishing human being formed from a clot, as a starting point for inquiry.
IBNASHUR:96:1/r13.anchor: وتوجيهه إلى النظر في خلق الله الموجودات وخاصة خلقه الإنسان خلقا عجيبا مستخرجا من علقة فذلك مبدأ النظر

IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.claim: Aisha's report is Ibn Ashur's basis for identifying these five verses as the first revelation to Muhammad in Hira.
IBNASHUR:96:1/r17.anchor: هذا أول ما أوحي به من القرآن إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ثبت عن عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR:96:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r1.claim: “He created the human from a clot” may be an explanatory apposition to “who created,” detailed after an implicit object, or a partitive apposition after a generic object; this order first establishes dependence on God, then reinforces the proof with detail.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r1.anchor: وسُلك طريق الإبدال لما فيه من الإجمال ابتداءً لإقامة الاستدلال على افتقار المخلوقات كلها إليه تعالى

IBNASHUR:96:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the clause can explain “who created,” if the first verb's object is understood from its clarification: the Lord who created the human from a clot.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون بياناً من { الذي خلق } إذا قُدر لفعل { خلق } الأول مفعول دل عليه بيانه

IBNASHUR:96:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r3.claim: The first “created” may be treated as intransitive, with its object omitted for generality (“all creation”), or with “the human” anticipated from the following clause.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r3.anchor: وعدم ذكر مفعول لفعل { خلق } يجوز أن يكون لتنزيل الفعل منزلة اللازم ، أي الذي هو الخالق

IBNASHUR:96:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r4.claim: Human creation is singled out because no one can overlook himself, making the question of who created him an especially immediate proof; 51:21 likewise directs people to themselves.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r4.anchor: لأنه المطَّرد في مقام الاستدلال إذ لا يَغفُلُ أحد من الناس عن نفسه ولا يخلو من أن يخطر له خاطر البحث

IBNASHUR:96:2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r5.claim: Mentioning human creation reproaches polytheists for missing God's oneness when its proof is present within themselves.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r5.anchor: وفيه تعريض بتحميق المشركين الذين ضلوا عن توحيد الله تعالى مع أن دليل الوحدانية قائم في أنفسهم

IBNASHUR:96:2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r6.claim: The phrase points to the wondrous developmental stages and qualities latent in human origins, from which the human becomes sovereign over the terrestrial world and capable of knowledge and writing.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r6.anchor: إشارة إلى ما ينطوي في أصل خَلْق الإِنسان من بديع الأطوار والصفات التي جعلته سلطانَ هذا العالم الأرضي

IBNASHUR:96:2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r7.claim: Alaq is the collective of alaqah: a fingertip-sized piece of thick, moist, congealed blood, named by resemblance to a small dark-red aquatic leech that attaches to animals and sucks blood.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r7.anchor: والعلق : اسم جمع عَلَقَة وهي قطعةٌ قَدرُ الأنملة من الدم الغليظ الجامد الباقي رطْباً لم يجفّ

IBNASHUR:96:2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r8.claim: After male and female reproductive fluids mix and time passes, they become a clot and embryonic development begins; the clot is named as the starting point because the male fluid alone cannot produce an embryo.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r8.anchor: ومعنى : { خلق الإنسان من علق } أن نطفة الذكر ونطفة المرأة بعد الاختلاط ومضي مدة كافيَة تصيران علقةً

IBNASHUR:96:2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur calls the mention of alaq a scientific miracle: he describes development from a microscopic ovum, its need to mix with male fluid, and its resemblance to an aquatic leech as it grows, linking the account to 22:5 and his tenth introduction.
IBNASHUR:96:2/r9.anchor: ومن إعجاز القرآن العلمي ذكر العلقة لأن الثابت في العلم الآن أن الإِنسان يتخلق من بويضة دقيقة جداً لا ترى إلا بالمرآة المكبِّرة

IBNASHUR:96:2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:2/r10.claim: Min here indicates beginning or origin.

IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.claim: These are the final verses of the five that were first revealed to Muhammad in the cave of Hira.
IBNASHUR:96:5/r8.anchor: وهذه آخر الخمس الآيات التي هي أول ما أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في غار حراء

IBNATIYYA:96:2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r1.claim: Human creation is an undeniable example, evident to innate perception, and among the greatest signs: no known creature offers more lessons in intellect, perception, bodily structure, and bones.
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r1.anchor: ثم مثل لهم من المخلوقات ما لا مدافعة فيه ،   وما يجده كل مفطور في نفسه ،   فقال : { خلق الإنسان من علق }

IBNATIYYA:96:2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r2.claim: ʿAlaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a small piece of blood.
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r2.anchor: والعلق جمع علقة ،   وهي القطعة اليسيرة من الدم

IBNATIYYA:96:2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r3.claim: Al-insān is generic here, and the mind extends the reference to all animals; it does not refer to Adam, who was created from clay.
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r3.anchor: و { الإنسان } هنا : اسم الجنس ،   ويمشي الذهن معه إلى جميع الحيوان ،   وليست الإشارة إلى آدم

IBNATIYYA:96:2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r4.claim: Since the unbelieving audience did not accept Adam's creation from clay as established, the verse leaves the original creation aside and uses the familiar human offspring to make the point accessible.
IBNATIYYA:96:2/r4.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك متقرراً عند الكفار المخاطبين بهذه الآية ،   فلذلك ترك أصل الخلقة وسيق لهم الفرع

IBNKATHIR:96:1/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r9.claim: The passage calls attention to humanity's beginning in a clinging clot.
IBNKATHIR:96:1/r9.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

IBNKATHIR:96:3/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:3/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:3/r8.claim: The passage calls attention to humanity's beginning in a clinging clot.
IBNKATHIR:96:3/r8.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

IBNKATHIR:96:4/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r8.claim: The passage calls attention to humanity's beginning in a clinging clot.
IBNKATHIR:96:4/r8.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

IBNKATHIR:96:5/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r8.claim: The passage calls attention to humanity's beginning in a clinging clot.
IBNKATHIR:96:5/r8.anchor: وفيها التنبيه على ابتداء خلق الإنسان من علقة

MAWARDI:96:2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:2/r1.claim: Here humankind means all people, created from a clot after the sperm-drop.
MAWARDI:96:2/r1.anchor: يريد بالإنسان جنس الناس كلهم ،   خلقوا من علق بعد النطفة ،

MAWARDI:96:2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:2/r2.claim: Alaq is the plural of ʿalaqa, a piece of wet blood named for sticking to what it touches; once dry, it is no longer a clot. A cited poem describes it clinging to the vein.
MAWARDI:96:2/r2.anchor: والعلقة قطعة من دم رطب سميت بذلك لأنها تعلق لرطوبتها بما تمر عليه ،   فإذا جفت لم تكن علقة

MAWARDI:96:2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:2/r3.claim: This can show God's bounty: from a lowly clot He made a sound, rational, discerning human being.
MAWARDI:96:2/r3.anchor: أن يبين قدر نعمته على الإنسان بأن خلقه من علقة مهينة حتى صار بشراً سوياً وعاقلاً متميزاً

MAWARDI:96:2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:2/r4.claim: It can also parallel God's moving the human from stage to stage with His moving the Prophet from ignorance to prophethood until he was fully prepared.
MAWARDI:96:2/r4.anchor: كذلك نقلك من الجهالة إلى النبوة حتى تستكمل محلها

NASAFI:96:2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:2/r1.claim: Humanity is singled out from all creation for its nobility and because revelation is addressed to it.
NASAFI:96:2/r1.anchor: تخصيص للإنسان بالذكر من بين ما يتناوله الخلق لشرفه ولأن التنزيل إليه

NASAFI:96:2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the wording first leaves the created thing unspecified and then identifies it as the human, magnifying the creation and its wondrous nature.
NASAFI:96:2/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد الذي خلق الإنسان إلا أنه ذكر مبهماً

NASAFI:96:2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:2/r3.claim: The plural “clots” is used instead of singular ʿalaqa because “human” has a collective sense.
NASAFI:96:2/r3.anchor: { مِنْ عَلَقٍ } وإنما جمع ولم يقل من علقة لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع

QURTUBI:96:2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r1.claim: The human means the son of Adam.
QURTUBI:96:2/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : " خلق الإنسان " يعني ابن آدم .

QURTUBI:96:2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r2.claim: Alaq is the plural of alaqa, a clotted blood; once blood flows it is called spilt blood.
QURTUBI:96:2/r2.anchor: " من علق " أي من دم ، جمع علقة ، والعلقة الدم الجامد

QURTUBI:96:2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r3.claim: The plural form is used because al-insan is generic: all humans are created from clots after the drop of semen.
QURTUBI:96:2/r3.anchor: فذكره بلفظ الجمع ؛ لأنه أراد بالإنسان الجمع ، وكلهم خلقوا من علق

QURTUBI:96:2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r4.claim: A clot is a moist piece of blood, named for clinging to what it touches; when it dries it is no longer called alaqa.
QURTUBI:96:2/r4.anchor: والعلقة : قطعة من دم رطب ، سميت بذلك لأنها تعلق لرطوبتها

QURTUBI:96:2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r5.claim: A cited poem describes blood from the heart's vital vein as علق, illustrating the word's sense of blood.
QURTUBI:96:2/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر : تركناه يخر على يديه

QURTUBI:96:2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:2/r6.claim: Humanity is singled out for honor by name.

QURTUBI:96:2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:2/r7.claim: Another explanation is that the verse displays God's favor: He made humans from a lowly clot and brought them to upright, rational maturity.
QURTUBI:96:2/r7.anchor: وقيل : أراد أن يبين قدر نعمته عليه ، بأن خلقه من علقة مهينة

RAZI:96:2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r1.claim: Rāzī offers a reading with no expressed object: God alone brings creation into being and reserves the act to Himself.
RAZI:96:2/r1.anchor: حصل منه الخلق واستأثر به لا خالق سواه

RAZI:96:2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the unrestricted object is every created thing; humanity is singled out as revelation’s recipient or the noblest creature on earth.

RAZI:96:2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r3.claim: Alternatively, the general statement about creation is clarified by human creation from a clot, magnifying its wondrous formation.
RAZI:96:2/r3.anchor: تفخيما لخلق الإنسان ودلالة على عجيب فطرته

RAZI:96:2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r4.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI:96:2/r4.claim: The theologians argue that God alone creates: creation uniquely distinguishes His essence, and divinity is the capacity to originate; Pharaoh’s question and Moses’ answer affirm this.
RAZI:96:2/r4.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بهذه الآية على أنه لا خالق غير الله تعالى

RAZI:96:2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r5.speaker: المتكلمون
RAZI:96:2/r5.claim: Theologians agree that the first obligation is knowing God, considering how to know Him, or intending that inquiry; they disagree over which formulation is correct.
RAZI:96:2/r5.anchor: اتفق المتكلمون على أن أول الواجبات معرفة الله تعالى

RAZI:96:2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r6.claim: Rāzī recounts how Abū Ḥanīfa sent Zufar to Basra, then advised him to present the opponents’ arguments before introducing his own, illustrating gradual persuasion.
RAZI:96:2/r6.anchor: إن زفر لما بعثه أبو حنيفة إلى البصرة

RAZI:96:2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r7.claim: God first leads idol worshippers to admit that He created them, then argues that an act requires an agent and idols cannot be creators because people carved them; this earns acknowledgment of God’s right to praise.
RAZI:96:2/r7.anchor: فبهذا التدريج يقرون بأني أنا المستحق للثناء دون الأوثان

RAZI:96:2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r8.claim: The argument excludes natural causation: a created cause needs another cause, while an eternal cause must either necessitate its effect or act by choice; ordered, beneficial change points to a knowing agent.
RAZI:96:2/r8.anchor: دلت الآية على أن القول بالطبع باطل

RAZI:96:2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:96:2/r9.claim: The plural ʿalaq is used because the generic word for humanity has collective force, as in the verse about humanity being in loss.

RAZI:96:3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r10.claim: The movement from the human’s lowly beginning as a clot to the highest created rank, knowledge, shows a directing and determining Lord; knowledge is humanity’s noblest trait.
RAZI:96:3/r10.anchor: أول أحوال الإنسان كونه علقة وهي أخس الأشياء

RAZI:96:3/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:3/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:96:3/r12.claim: The opening reference to the Lord who created humanity from a clot provides a rational proof of divine power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy.
RAZI:96:3/r12.anchor: الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة
